lessons.title: Why we prune and the tools we use
lessons.html:
Why we prune and the tools we use

Pruning means cutting off parts of a plant. We prune shrubs to keep them healthy, neat and full of flowers.

Why we prune

  • To remove dead, sick or broken branches.
  • To keep a nice shape and the right size.
  • To make the shrub grow thicker, like a hedge.
  • To get more flowers.
  • To keep paths, windows and doors clear.
  • To let light and air into the middle of the shrub. This helps stop disease.

Pruning tools

ToolUsed for
SecateursThin stems, up to about the thickness of a finger
Loppers (long-handled)Thicker branches
Pruning sawThick branches
Hedge shearsShaping hedges
Electric or petrol hedge trimmerLarge hedges, by trained workers only

Look after your tools

  • Keep blades sharp. Blunt tools tear stems and let disease in.
  • Clean blades after each job. When cutting sick plants, clean the blades with disinfectant before you move to the next plant.
  • Oil the tools and store them dry.
  • Keep secateurs closed and locked when you are not using them.

Safety

Wear gloves, safety glasses and boots. Some shrubs have thorns, like roses and bougainvillea. Never cut towards your body or your other hand. Use a stable ladder only if you are trained, and never stand on the top step. Keep hedge trimmer cables behind you, and switch off before clearing branches from the blade.

lessons.title: How to prune and shape
lessons.html:
How to prune and shape

The 3 Ds first

Always start by cutting out the 3 Ds:

  • Dead branches
  • Diseased (sick) branches
  • Damaged (broken) branches

Also cut out branches that cross and rub against each other.

Making a good cut

  1. Find a bud. A bud is a small bump on the stem where a new shoot will grow.
  2. Choose a bud that faces outwards, away from the middle of the shrub.
  3. Cut just above the bud, about half a centimetre above it.
  4. Cut at a small slope, so rain runs off away from the bud.
  5. Do not leave long stumps. Stumps die and rot.
  6. Do not cut too close to the bud. It can dry out.

Shaping

  • Step back often and look at the whole shrub. Is the shape even?
  • For a hedge, make it a little wider at the bottom than at the top. Then light reaches the lower leaves and the hedge stays thick.
  • Do not cut off more than about a third of the shrub at one time, unless your team leader tells you.

When to prune

Different shrubs are pruned at different times. Many shrubs that flower in spring are pruned just after flowering. Roses are usually pruned in late winter. Your team leader will tell you when. Pruning at the wrong time can cut off next season's flowers.

Clean up

Rake up all cut branches and leaves. Put healthy material on the compost or in the chipper. Put sick material in the rubbish, not the compost.

Key points

  • Prune for health, shape, size and more flowers.
  • Keep tools sharp and clean; disinfect after sick plants.
  • Cut dead, diseased and damaged branches first.
  • Cut just above an outward-facing bud, at a slope.
  • Ask your team leader when to prune each shrub.
